title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Corinthians chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Corinthians Chapter 4.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The god of this world hath blinded
God commanded the light to shine out of darkness
questions.correctAnswer: We have received mercy
questions.explanation: This phrase is found in 2 Corinthians 4:1, which states 'as we have received mercy'.

questions.question: What have we renounced according to 2 Corinthians 4?
options: The light of the glorious gospel
The knowledge of the glory of God
questions.correctAnswer: The hidden things of dishonesty
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Corinthians 4:2, which mentions having 'renounced the hidden things of dishonesty'.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 4, who is blinded by the god of this world?
questions.correctAnswer: Them that are lost
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:3 states, 'But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost.'

questions.question: What does the god of this world do to the minds of those who believe not?
questions.correctAnswer: He blinds them
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:4 states that the god of this world 'hath blinded the minds of them which believe not'.

questions.question: Who do we preach according to 2 Corinthians 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Christ Jesus the Lord
questions.explanation: This is clearly stated in 2 Corinthians 4:5, which says, 'For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord.'

questions.question: What has God commanded according to 2 Corinthians 4?
options: The light to shine out of darkness
questions.correctAnswer: The light to shine out of darkness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:6 mentions that 'God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness'.

questions.question: What does God give us according to 2 Corinthians 4?
options: The knowledge of the glory of God
questions.correctAnswer: The knowledge of the glory of God
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:6 states that God has shined in our hearts 'to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God'.

questions.question: Who is the image of God according to 2 Corinthians 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:4 refers to Christ as 'the image of God'.

questions.question: What does Paul say about the truth in 2 Corinthians 4?
options: It is hidden from the lost
It commends ourselves to every man's conscience
questions.correctAnswer: It commends ourselves to every man's conscience
questions.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 4:2, it states 'but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man's conscience'.

questions.question: What should we not do according to 2 Corinthians 4:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Walk in craftiness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:2 states, 'not walking in craftiness'.

questions.question: What is the result of the gospel being hid according to 2 Corinthians 4?
options: It is hidden to those who believe
It is hidden to those who are lost
questions.correctAnswer: It is hidden to those who are lost
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:3 states, 'But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost.'

questions.question: Is it true that we faint not according to 2 Corinthians 4?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:1 states, 'we faint not'.

questions.question: Is it true that we handle the word of God deceitfully according to 2 Corinthians 4?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:2 states we do not handle the word of God deceitfully.

questions.question: Is it false that the light of the glorious gospel is hidden from the believers according to 2 Corinthians 4?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:3 states that the gospel is hid to them that are lost, not believers.

questions.question: Is it false that the light shines in our hearts according to 2 Corinthians 4?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:6 states that God has shined in our hearts to give light.

medium.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Corinthians Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 4:7, why do we have treasure in earthen vessels?
options: That the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us
To show our own strength and wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: That the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:7 explains that the treasure is in earthen vessels so that the power displayed is from God and not from ourselves.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 4:8 promise will happen if someone trusts God despite being troubled on every side as mentioned in 2 Corinthians 4:7?
options: They will be perplexed, but not in despair
They will have no troubles at all
They will be completely free from persecution
They will become strong and never cast down
questions.correctAnswer: They will be perplexed, but not in despair
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:8 states that even though we are troubled on every side, we are not in despair, showing a promise of sustaining faith after trusting God as described in 4:7.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 4:9 say about those who are persecuted and cast down?
options: They are not forsaken and not destroyed
They will be forsaken and destroyed
They will be victorious without struggle
They will be forgotten and defeated
questions.correctAnswer: They are not forsaken and not destroyed
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:9 states that though persecuted and cast down, believers are not forsaken or destroyed, affirming God's sustaining power.

questions.question: How do 2 Corinthians 4:10 and 2 Corinthians 4:11 connect the experience of suffering with the manifestation of Jesus' life?
options: Bearing about the dying of Jesus in the body shows life also of Jesus manifested in our mortal flesh
Suffering is unrelated to the life of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Bearing about the dying of Jesus in the body shows life also of Jesus manifested in our mortal flesh
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 connect the ongoing experience of suffering (dying) with the life of Jesus being made visible in believers’ mortal bodies.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 4:12 reveal about the relationship between death and life in believers?
options: Death works in us, but life works in you
Death and life both work only in us
Life works in us, death works in you
Neither death nor life affects believers
questions.correctAnswer: Death works in us, but life works in you
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:12 explains the paradox that while death operates in the apostles, life is effected in the believers.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 4:1, what is the attitude of those who have received mercy and the ministry?
questions.correctAnswer: They faint not
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:1 states that those who have received mercy and the ministry do not faint, indicating perseverance.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 4:2 describe the manner in which the word of God should be handled?
options: Not handling the word of God deceitfully
questions.correctAnswer: Not handling the word of God deceitfully
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:2 instructs believers to renounce dishonesty and not to handle God's word deceitfully.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 4:3 say about the gospel being hidden?
options: It is hidden to those who are lost
It is not hidden to anyone
It is hidden only to believers
questions.correctAnswer: It is hidden to those who are lost
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:3 explains that if the gospel is hidden, it is hidden specifically to those who are lost.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 4:4, who blinds the minds of those who do not believe?
questions.correctAnswer: The god of this world
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:4 identifies 'the god of this world' as the one who blinds the minds of unbelievers.

questions.question: What is the purpose of God shining light in our hearts as stated in 2 Corinthians 4:6?
options: To give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ
To make us rich and famous
To hide the truth from others
questions.correctAnswer: To give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:6 describes God's purpose in shining light in our hearts as revealing the knowledge of His glory in Jesus Christ.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 4:5 describe the apostles' role in preaching?
options: They preach not themselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: They preach not themselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:5 states that the apostles preach Christ and serve people for Jesus' sake, not themselves.

questions.question: What practical attitude can believers learn from 2 Corinthians 4:8-9 about handling trials?
options: Be troubled but not distressed, persecuted but not forsaken
Avoid all troubles at any cost
questions.correctAnswer: Be troubled but not distressed, persecuted but not forsaken
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:8-9 teaches believers to endure troubles with resilience, showing trust in God's sustaining power.

questions.question: How does the metaphor of 'earthen vessels' in 2 Corinthians 4:7 apply to Christian living?
options: It shows human weakness that carries God's power
It suggests Christians should seek earthly treasures
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human weakness that carries God's power
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:7 uses 'earthen vessels' to illustrate human frailty as the container for God's power, encouraging humility and reliance on God.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 4:10, believers always carry about in their bodies the dying of the Lord Jesus so that His life might be made manifest in them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:10 clearly states that believers bear in their bodies the dying of Jesus to reveal His life.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Corinthians 4:12, death works in believers while life works in those outside the church.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:12 states death works in the apostles (us) and life works in the believers (you), not the other way around.

hard.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Corinthians Chapter 4.

questions.question: What is the spirit of faith mentioned in 2 Corinthians 4:13 associated with?
options: I believed, and therefore have I spoken
We are troubled on every side
questions.correctAnswer: I believed, and therefore have I spoken
questions.explanation: This is directly cited in 2 Corinthians 4:13, where Paul references the spirit of faith in relation to believing and speaking.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 4:14, what assurance do we have regarding the resurrection?
options: He which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also
questions.correctAnswer: He which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also
questions.explanation: This promise is found in 2 Corinthians 4:14, emphasizing the connection between Jesus' resurrection and our own.

questions.question: In 2 Corinthians 4:15, what is the purpose of all things according to Paul?
options: That the abundant grace might redound to the glory of God
To show the light of the knowledge of God
questions.correctAnswer: That the abundant grace might redound to the glory of God
questions.explanation: This is stated in 2 Corinthians 4:15, indicating that all things serve to glorify God through grace.

questions.question: What does 2 Corinthians 4:16 say about the outward and inward man?
options: The inward man is renewed day by day
questions.correctAnswer: The inward man is renewed day by day
questions.explanation: This is explicitly mentioned in 2 Corinthians 4:16, contrasting the perishing outward man with the renewing inward man.

questions.question: According to 2 Corinthians 4:17, how does Paul describe our afflictions?
questions.correctAnswer: They are light and momentary
questions.explanation: Paul describes our afflictions in 2 Corinthians 4:17 as light and temporary, emphasizing their transient nature compared to eternal glory.

questions.question: What contrast does 2 Corinthians 4:18 present regarding what is seen and unseen?
questions.correctAnswer: The seen is temporal
questions.explanation: This contrast in 2 Corinthians 4:18 highlights that what is seen is temporary while the unseen is eternal.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'pistis' in 2 Corinthians 4:13 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith
questions.explanation: 'Pistis' is the Greek word for faith, reflecting the trust and belief that Paul speaks of in 2 Corinthians 4:13.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily employed in 2 Corinthians 4:16-18?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Parallelism is used in 2 Corinthians 4:16-18 as Paul contrasts the outward and inward man and the seen and unseen.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of resurrection found in 2 Corinthians 4:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 6:5
questions.explanation: Romans 6:5 connects with the theme of resurrection from the dead, resonating with the assurance in 2 Corinthians 4:14.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the concept of light in 2 Corinthians 4:6?
questions.correctAnswer: John 8:12
questions.explanation: John 8:12 connects with the theme of Jesus as the light, similar to the light mentioned in 2 Corinthians 4:6.

questions.question: What comes before 2 Corinthians 4:13?
questions.correctAnswer: We renounce hidden things
questions.explanation: The verse immediately preceding 2 Corinthians 4:13 is about renouncing hidden things of dishonesty, found in 2 Corinthians 4:2.

questions.question: What comes after 2 Corinthians 4:16?
questions.correctAnswer: For our light affliction
questions.explanation: The verse following 2 Corinthians 4:16 is 2 Corinthians 4:17, which discusses light affliction.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in the phrase 'light affliction' in 2 Corinthians 4:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Euphemism
questions.explanation: 'Light affliction' is a euphemism in 2 Corinthians 4:17, contrasting the gravity of suffering with the glory to come.

questions.question: The statement that 'we faint not' in 2 Corinthians 4:1 implies resilience in the face of trials. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:1 states that despite challenges, Paul emphasizes not losing heart, indicating resilience.

questions.question: The inward man perishing indicates a lack of hope in 2 Corinthians 4:16. True or False?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:16 indicates the inward man is renewed, suggesting hope despite the outward man's perishing.

theological.title: 2 Corinthians Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Corinthians Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 4:2 teach about the nature of Christian ministry?
options: Ministry must be conducted with honesty and transparency, renouncing deceit
Ministry should rely on human wisdom and craftiness to succeed
Ministry is primarily about gaining worldly honor and recognition
Ministry involves hiding the truth to protect the vulnerable
questions.correctAnswer: Ministry must be conducted with honesty and transparency, renouncing deceit
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:2 teaches that Christian ministry involves renouncing hidden dishonesty and not handling the word of God deceitfully, emphasizing honesty and transparency.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 4:4 teach about spiritual blindness?
options: The god of this world blinds the minds of unbelievers to prevent them seeing the gospel
Spiritual blindness is a natural human condition unrelated to demonic influence
All people have equal access to the knowledge of Christ without spiritual obstruction
Spiritual blindness is caused by lack of intellectual capacity
questions.correctAnswer: The god of this world blinds the minds of unbelievers to prevent them seeing the gospel
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:4 states that 'the god of this world' blinds the minds of unbelievers so that the light of the gospel does not shine on them, highlighting a spiritual warfare reality.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of Christ in preaching is taught in 2 Corinthians 4:5?
options: Preaching is not about ourselves but about Christ Jesus as Lord
Preachers must exalt themselves to gain followers
The gospel message is secondary to the preacher’s charisma
Preaching should avoid mentioning Christ directly to appeal to all
questions.correctAnswer: Preaching is not about ourselves but about Christ Jesus as Lord
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:5 affirms that preaching centers on Christ Jesus, not on the preacher, who serves for Jesus’ sake.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Corinthians 4:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:6 shows God's sovereign power in commanding light to shine out of darkness and shining in believers' hearts the knowledge of His glory.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in 2 Corinthians 4:7 by describing the treasure in earthen vessels?
questions.correctAnswer: Power
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:7 highlights that the excellency of the power belongs to God, as the treasure is held in fragile vessels, demonstrating divine power working through human weakness.

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 4:10 connect to the larger biblical theme of Christ's sufferings?
options: It teaches believers share in Christ’s sufferings so His life is manifested in them
It denies that believers should suffer for Christ’s sake
It portrays suffering as meaningless and disconnected from Christ
It emphasizes that only Christ suffered, not His followers
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches believers share in Christ’s sufferings so His life is manifested in them
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:10 describes bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus to manifest His life, connecting to the biblical doctrine of believers’ participation in Christ’s sufferings (cf. Romans 8:17).

questions.question: How does 2 Corinthians 4:14 relate to the resurrection hope presented elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It affirms that believers will be raised up by Jesus just as He was raised
It teaches that resurrection is purely metaphorical and not bodily
It denies any future resurrection for believers
It claims resurrection depends on human works
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that believers will be raised up by Jesus just as He was raised
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:14 teaches that the one who raised Jesus will also raise believers, aligning with the New Testament hope of bodily resurrection (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:20-22).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 16 and 18 teach about sanctification and hope?
options: Though the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed daily by focusing on eternal unseen realities
Physical decay means spiritual decay and loss of hope
Sanctification is solely about outward behavior without inner renewal
Focusing on temporal things is the key to spiritual growth
questions.correctAnswer: Though the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed daily by focusing on eternal unseen realities
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:16 and 18 together teach that inward spiritual renewal happens daily despite physical decline, because believers fix their eyes on eternal unseen things rather than temporal visible ones.

questions.question: What doctrine about suffering and glory do verses 17 and 18 jointly teach?
options: Present affliction is temporary and produces an eternal weight of glory
Suffering has no redemptive value and should be avoided at all costs
Glory is only earthly and visible, not eternal
Affliction is permanent and leads to despair
questions.correctAnswer: Present affliction is temporary and produces an eternal weight of glory
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:17-18 teaches that current light afflictions are momentary and result in a far more exceeding and eternal glory, highlighting the redemptive value of suffering.

questions.question: What combined teaching about Christian witness and suffering is found in verses 8 and 9?
options: Believers face troubles and persecution but are sustained and not destroyed by God’s power
Troubles cause believers to be forsaken and destroyed
Christian suffering is a sign of divine rejection
Believers are always free from distress and persecution
questions.correctAnswer: Believers face troubles and persecution but are sustained and not destroyed by God’s power
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:8-9 explains that though believers are troubled and persecuted, they are not in despair or destroyed, indicating God’s sustaining grace amid suffering.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that the gospel is ineffective because it is hidden from many. What does 2 Corinthians 4:3-4 actually teach?
options: The gospel is hidden to those who are lost because the god of this world blinds their minds
The gospel is hidden because God does not want all to be saved
The gospel is only for a select few and is intentionally withheld
The gospel message is unclear and confusing, causing it to be hidden
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel is hidden to those who are lost because the god of this world blinds their minds
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:3-4 teaches that the gospel is hidden to the lost because the god of this world blinds their minds, highlighting spiritual blindness rather than gospel ineffectiveness.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Corinthians 4:13 teach about faith and proclamation?
options: Belief in God leads to speaking boldly, as faith and speech are linked
Faith is private and should not be publicly proclaimed
Speech is independent of faith and relies on human rhetoric
Believers must wait for perfect certainty before speaking
questions.correctAnswer: Belief in God leads to speaking boldly, as faith and speech are linked
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:13 states that having the spirit of faith leads believers to speak, linking belief with proclamation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated in 2 Corinthians 4:14 regarding resurrection?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:14 emphasizes God's faithfulness in raising Jesus and promising to raise believers also, demonstrating His covenantal faithfulness.

questions.question: How do 2 Corinthians 4:1 and 16 together teach about perseverance in ministry?
options: Mercy empowers ministry so believers do not faint despite outward weakness, as inward renewal sustains them
Ministry should cease when the outward man perishes
Perseverance depends solely on human strength and endurance
Fainting is inevitable and indicates failure in ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy empowers ministry so believers do not faint despite outward weakness, as inward renewal sustains them
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:1 speaks of ministry sustained by mercy without fainting, and verse 16 shows inward renewal despite outward decay, together teaching perseverance through God’s grace.

questions.question: What theological significance does 2 Corinthians 4:12 hold about the relationship between Christian suffering and the life of others?
options: Death works in believers so that life might work in others
Suffering is a purely individual experience with no corporate impact
Death and life are unrelated in Christian experience
Believers avoid death so others can live
questions.correctAnswer: Death works in believers so that life might work in others
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 4:12 teaches that the deaths believers endure produce spiritual life in others, indicating the redemptive, communal dimension of Christian suffering.
